text:
maya-devx: Hey team — customer 'Acme AI' private inference VPC can't reach our model registry over TLS. Apps see ECONNRESET during handshake. Started ~0900 UTC after security team applied firewall hardening. Can someone triage? attaching quick tcpdump + curl output below.

maya-devx: tcpdump (filtered):
  10:12:01.123 IP 10.0.3.12.52344 > 3.5.6.7.443: SYN
  10:12:01.125 IP 3.5.6.7.443 > 10.0.3.12.52344: RST, ack 1

maya-devx: curl -vk --resolve models.redwood.example.net:443:3.5.6.7 https://models.redwood.example.net/
  * About to connect() to models.redwood.example.net port 443 (#0)
  *   Trying 3.5.6.7...
  * Connected to models.redwood.example.net (3.5.6.7) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS handshake -> received RST, connection reset

ian-support: Thanks. Is this Dedicated or Private? Which region/az? Any recent security group or NACL changes (rule ids)?

maya-devx: Private/VPC (customer-managed controls) in eu-west-1, AZ b. Security team said they applied NACL hardening Friday (ticket SEC-412). No SG changes from our side.

siva-enginfra: FYI: NACLs are stateless so if there's a DENY or missing allow for ephemeral return ports you will see server-side RSTs / failed handshakes. Can you paste `aws ec2 describe-network-acls` for that subnet and `aws ec2 describe-security-groups` for the instances? Also run a quick netcat from the node: `nc -vz 3.5.6.7 443` and `ss -tn state established` during attempt.

maya-devx: Pasted excerpts: NACL entries (ordered):
  rule 100: ALLOW TCP 80 0.0.0.0/0
  rule 110: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0
  rule 120: DENY ALL 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0
  egress rule 100: ALLOW TCP 80
  egress rule 110: ALLOW TCP 443
  egress rule 120: DENY ALL 1024-65535

maya-devx: SG egress: 0.0.0.0/0 tcp 443 allowed. NAT gateway SG allows 1024-65535.

alex-sre: Aha — NACL has an explicit DENY for ephemeral range (1024-65535). Because NACLs are stateless the return path for ephemeral client ports gets dropped. That will produce SYN->RST behavior like you're seeing.

alex-sre: Quick repro idea: from host run `sudo hping3 -S -p 443 3.5.6.7 --count 1 --baseport 52344` and watch for RSTs. But main fix: either remove/modify the NACL DENY rule or add explicit ALLOW rules for ephemeral ranges (order matters: lower-number rules evaluated first).

ian-support: Two operational options: 1) Add NACL ALLOW for ephemeral TCP 1024-65535 (rule number <120) for both inbound and outbound; 2) If security policy prohibits that, create a VPC endpoint (private link) for models.redwood.example.net so traffic doesn't traverse NACL/NAT path. Also consider an exception to maintain TLS integrity.

maya-devx: We tried temporarily inserting ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 at rule 115 (inbound+outbound) — curl now completes the handshake and we get 200.

siva-enginfra: Good. Root cause: NACL rule ordering + deny-all ephemeral. Follow-up items:
  - Add automated check in onboarding docs to ensure no NACL denies ephemeral range
  - Recommend customers prefer stateful SG egress on NATs or VPC endpoints for model registry
  - For teams that must keep strict NACLs, provide explicit snippet to insert rules with correct priorities.

alex-sre: Suggested CLI snippet to add rule (example):
  aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-12345 --rule-number 115 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0

deploy-bot: Change scheduled: NACL entry 115 added (automated rollback 10m) by ops-runner.

maya-devx: Verified after change — customer confirmed inference calls stable and no more TLS ECONNRESET. Closing on our side. Can we capture this in a short postmortem and add a note to our Private deployment checklist? :+1:

ian-support: Filing postmortem stub and action items (PM-890). Thanks everyone.
